cells.tense: You are here, at the table, with the pen still moving in your hand.
cells.act: teach it the way it was taught to you, with one change
cells.ask: Show someone the way you read a table and shift what you give — the way you learned it, with a piece changed to be your own.
cells.core:
You can sit where several people want different things and keep your footing. Something in you tracks who has been heard and who has not, and adjusts what you give until it fits, then adjusts again. That is not a middle point you find and hold. It is work, done in the open, and it leaves each person with their share.

What that work is worth is easier to see from outside than from in. Think of the way you take a table's temperature, the way you hand something over. Somebody taught you that, or you picked it up watching. Show the shape of it this week to one person the way you got it, with a piece changed. The change is yours, and so is the skill. When it leaves your hands it should still be recognisable as yours.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the table level by working at it.
cells.verb: reading the room and adjusting what you give until it fits
cells.place: at the table where what each person is owed gets settled

cells.tense: You will have smoothed things over before anyone has said what they actually want.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Take one step today toward what you actually want, before you feel ready, and leave the friction where it falls.
cells.core:
You read a table fast. Before anyone disagrees, you can feel which way the conversation is heading, and you get there first — soften the edge, agree before the other person finishes, keep the peace while it is still cheap. Harmony arrives early. So does the thing it cost.

Differences that would have been useful stay unsaid, and after a while the ground you keep smooth is one where nobody says what they want, including you. The calm is real. It is just thinner than it looks. So move the other way once: pick what you want and take a step toward it today, before you feel ready, with the friction left where it falls, and find out whether the peace you have been keeping can survive a fact.

cells.tense: You were scattered by each thing that came at you, and you are still there.
cells.act: let yourself be reached by what they are carrying
cells.ask: Next time someone near you is carrying something, let it reach you for a minute — feel it with them, without fixing it and without losing where you end.
cells.core:
Where more than one person is talking at once, you get pulled apart. Someone is upset, someone wants something, someone disagrees, and each takes a piece of your attention until there is no center left to read from. You were scattered by the last thing that arrived. The skill is in you — you can track a table. Right now it has nothing steady to stand on.

Pushing harder at the tracking won't give the center back. Contact will. Next time someone near you is carrying something, let it reach you — for a minute, feel what they are feeling, without fixing it and without disappearing into it. Your own side stays yours. That move puts something under the reading. Do it once, and you will know what it feels like to be at the table rather than scattered across it.

cells.tense: You are already adjusting what you give, and you would say the room just runs that way.
cells.act: hand one thing on in the way you were handed it
cells.ask: Pass to someone the move you make to keep a table level — the way it came to you — and notice that you picked the moment.
cells.core:
You are the one who notices who hasn't spoken, who shifts what you give so the quiet one gets room and the loud one gets heard. Ask you about it and you would say the room just runs that way. The adjustments are yours. Nobody assigned them. The reading is happening, and the author's name is not on it.

So put a name on it, small. Pass to someone the move you make to keep a table on its feet, the way it came to you — the way you learned it, from whoever it was. Do it once, and notice that you picked the moment. The gap isn't skill. It's seeing that the hand on the dial has been yours the entire time. You were already doing the work. Now you get to see it.

attempts.check: The draft risks claiming I know what a particular argument at their table is about, which the record does not support — so each cell stays with the moment of reading the room and what the person reaches for there. A reader could say the calibration they do is simply good manners, not avoidance; the Too Much ask survives that, since tracing the last three smoothings works even if only one was a real flinch, and the Balancer ask works even if they call it ordinary tact. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line about them being 'the one who keeps everyone okay' — that is a role I invented, so it stays out.
